run.head: 76ef33f44a600c3ed1a385979fd1dfbcade3fbb6
run.change_description:
grpc: hold ac.mu while calling resetTransport to prevent concurrent connection attempts

This change ensures that caller of resetTransport() keep holding the mutex instead of releasing it and having resetTransport() re-acquire it. This ensures that no concurrent requests are able to start once caller of resetTransport does some validation and calls resetTransport.

See https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/7365#issuecomment-2208258873 for more details.

Tested: Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts with the change.

Fixes: https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/7365

RELEASE NOTES:
- client: fix race that could lead to orphaned connections and associated resources.

summary.intent: Hold `ac.mu` across the Idle-to-Connecting transition (rename `resetTransport` to `resetTransportAndUnlock`) so `addrConn.connect()` and `addrConn.updateAddrs()` can no longer race into two concurrent connection attempts, fixing the flaky `Test/AuthorityRevive` and the underlying orphaned-transport leak described in grpc/grpc-go#7365.
summary.issue_fit: Met — the race window between the Idle check and the Connecting state transition is closed by keeping ac.mu locked across both; a fresh-context verifier confirmed both the atomicity of that transition and that every return path of resetTransportAndUnlock() still releases the lock. Source: originating issues; user-supplied spec; commit messages in the range.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (clientconn.go, +6/-7, the only changed file); both call sites of resetTransport/resetTransportAndUnlock (connect(), updateAddrs()) and their single caller (balancer_wrapper.go) inspected at base and head; focused test `go test -race -run 'Test/^AuthorityRevive$' -count=100 ./xds/internal/xdsclient/tests/` run once at the reviewed head: pass (13.8s).

tasks.premise: ac.mu is held continuously from the Idle check in connect() (clientconn.go:906-921) through the Connecting transition inside resetTransportAndUnlock() (clientconn.go:1234-1262), so no second call to connect() can observe ac.state == Idle and start a duplicate resetTransportAndUnlock() while the first caller's transition to Connecting is still pending.

resetTransportAndUnlock() unlocks ac.mu on every return path, and updateAddrs() (clientconn.go:996) hands off the already-locked ac.mu to a new goroutine running resetTransportAndUnlock() without an intervening unlock, so this handoff never leaves ac.mu permanently locked or produces a double-unlock/unlock-of-unlocked-mutex panic.
